title: Conserved and divergent gene regulatory programs of the mammalian neocortex.
authors: Zemke, Nathan R; Armand, Ethan J; Wang, Wenliang; Lee, Seoyeon; Zhou, Jingtian; Li, Yang Eric; Liu, Hanqing; Tian, Wei; Nery, Joseph R; Castanon, Rosa G; Bartlett, Anna; Osteen, Julia K; Li, Daofeng; Zhuo, Xiaoyu; Xu, Vincent; Chang, Lei; Dong, Keyi; Indralingam, Hannah S; Rink, Jonathan A; Xie, Yang; Miller, Michael; Krienen, Fenna M; Zhang, Qiangge; Taskin, Naz; Ting, Jonathan; Feng, Guoping; McCarroll, Steven A; Callaway, Edward M; Wang, Ting; Lein, Ed S; Behrens, M Margarita; Ecker, Joseph R; Ren, Bing
one_liner_zh: 该文利用单细胞多组学与机器学习预测顺式调控元件，研究哺乳动物新皮层基因调控程序的保守与分化，涉及转录因子表达与表观基因组关联，但核心是调控元件注释而非TF-DNA结合机制建模，方法可迁移但深度有限。
abstract: Divergence of cis-regulatory elements drives species-specific traits(1), but how this manifests in the evolution of the neocortex at the molecular and cellular level remains unclear. Here we investigated the gene regulatory programs in the primary motor cortex of human, macaque, marmoset and mouse using single-cell multiomics assays, generating gene expression, chromatin accessibility, DNA methylome and chromosomal conformation profiles from a total of over 200,000 cells. From these data, we show evidence that divergence of transcription factor expression corresponds to species-specific epigenome landscapes. We find that conserved and divergent gene regulatory features are reflected in the evolution of the three-dimensional genome. Transposable elements contribute to nearly 80% of the human-specific candidate cis-regulatory elements in cortical cells. Through machine learning, we develop sequence-based predictors of candidate cis-regulatory elements in different species and demonstrate that the genomic regulatory syntax is highly preserved from rodents to primates. Finally, we show that epigenetic conservation combined with sequence similarity helps to uncover functional cis-regulatory elements and enhances our ability to interpret genetic variants contributing to neurological disease and traits.
abstract_zh: 顺式调控元件的分化驱动了物种特异性性状(1)，但这一过程如何在分子和细胞水平上体现于新皮层的进化中，仍不清楚。在此，我们利用单细胞多组学技术，研究了人类、猕猴、绒猴和小鼠初级运动皮层中的基因调控程序，从总计超过20万个细胞中生成了基因表达、染色质可及性、DNA甲基化组和染色体构象图谱。从这些数据中，我们展示了转录因子表达的分化与物种特异性表观基因组景观相对应的证据。我们发现，保守和分化的基因调控特征反映在三维基因组的进化中。转座元件贡献了皮层细胞中近80%的人类特异性候选顺式调控元件。通过机器学习，我们开发了基于序列的不同物种候选顺式调控元件预测器，并证明基因组调控语法在从啮齿类到灵长类中高度保守。最后，我们表明，表观遗传保守性与序列相似性相结合，有助于揭示功能性顺式调控元件，并增强我们解读与神经系统疾病和性状相关的遗传变异的能力。
